input: A shell-and-tube exchanger located in a refinery preheat train is used to heat propylene glycol. It may be noted that the propylene glycol is being heated as part of the preheat duty of the train, and that the exchanger is one item within that train rather than a standalone unit. The duty of the exchanger is 732 kW. The hot stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C, while the cold stream enters at 35 °C and leaves at 50 °C. For these terminal temperatures, the log-mean temperature difference works out at 111.6 K. With an installed area of 24.8 m2, the overall coefficient is 265 W m-2 K-1. The terminal temperatures fix the temperature programme of the unit: the hot stream gives up the stated duty across its stated fall in temperature, and the cold stream takes up the same duty across its corresponding rise. It is worth noting that the coefficient is stated on the basis of the installed area: it is the duty divided by the product of the area and the log-mean temperature difference, and it conveniently covers the resistance of both films and the wall in a single figure. The coefficient should be understood as an as-found figure for the run reported, and it will be expected to move as fouling builds up on the surfaces over time. Fouling was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run. No cleaning cycle has yet been completed, and the assessment therefore covers one run from the start of service; fouling behaviour over repeated runs separated by cleaning is not covered by the assessment.
